tossups.text: A set of these points that are characterized by the birth of closed invariant curves and can lead to the formation of a torus in limit-cycle maps is named for Neimark and Sacker. For systems generated by a set of autonomous ordinary differential equations, one of these points occurs when critical equilibrium has exactly one zero eigenvalue. If several branches have an equilibrium point at which the Jacobian is zero, the equilibrium point is classified as one of these points. These points are defined to be "supercritical" if they lead to the development of stabilizing cycles. These occurrences come in a "pitchfork" type and one sometimes co-named for Poincare and Andronov. For 10 points, give this term that denotes points representing the sudden appearance of qualitatively different solutions, one of which is named for Hopf.

A namesake park in Kelleys Island, Ohio, provides an excellent example of the "scratches" created by these things. These objects sometimes feature large columns called seracs. Lake Agassiz was formed by the action of these entities before being drained by a series of events known as jökulhlaups. Their mass balance depends on the ratio of the rates of accumulation and ablation. When two of these objects are near each other, they can create sharply ridged arêtes which rise up between U-shaped valleys. These entities create piles of debris known as moraines, and erosion caused by them creates fjords. For 10 points, name these massive, slow-moving sheets of ice.

This part of a cell may have been developed by cells absorbing bacteria. It is surrounded by a double membrane, and produces ATP for the cell. This part of a cell has a key role in processing nutrients taken in by the cell and converting them to energy. For 10 points, name this "powerhouse" of the cell.

One painting from this movement shows the title figure's hair sprawled across a large bowl in which she has hidden her lover's severed head. Mary offers her cheek to a recently wounded boy Jesus in one work from this movement. One artist from this movement showed a group of neglected sheep wander into a corn field in the background as their shepherd shows a moth to a young girl in The Hireling Shepherd. Elizabeth Siddal served as the model for Beata Beatrix and Ophelia, which were painted by this movement's John Everett Millais and Dante Gabriel Rossetti, respectively. For 10 points, name this movement which sought to take art back to a time before its corruption by a Renaissance artist.

In female children, this disorder is often confused for Rett's syndrome. Children with this disorder are shown to lack a properly developed theory-of-mind in the Sally-Anne test. Ramachandran proposed that this disorder was caused by broken mirror neurons. Simon Baron-Cohen explained this disorder by describing an "extreme male brain." Leo Kanner proposed that this disorder was the result of neglectful "refrigerator mothers." A fraudulent Lancet article by Andrew Wakefield claimed that this disorder was caused by vaccinations. For 10 points, Asperger's syndrome is a form of what disorder characterized by challenges with social skills?

The Blue and Green demes [deems] were fans of this sport who clashed in the Nika Riots, which began in the Hippodrome of Constantinople. Gaius Appuleius Diocles [gah-yuss ah-poo-lee-us dye-oh-kleez] became the wealthiest athlete in history by operating a quadriga in this sport. Ancient Olympic prizes for this sport were given to the owner, not the driver. Rome's Circus Maximus held competitions of, for 10 points, what sporting event involving horse-drawn vehicles?

An early type of apartment-style housing known as rab' surrounded this city's synagogue, whose genizah (geh-NEE-zuh) contains over 400,000 medieval manuscripts. This city's Circassian Burji dynasty was succeeded by the Turkic Bahri dynasty. This city's port of Fariskur was the site of Louis IX's capture during the Seventh Crusade. The former capital of Fustat was replaced by this city, where a citadel was built by the Ayyubids. This city is home to the Al-Azhar Mosque. The Fatimid Caliphate ruled from, for 10 points, what Egyptian city?

It has nothing to do with Robert Walpole, but Section II of this legislation mandated the creation of a sinking fund. An ambiguity in this piece of legislation led to the Supreme Court case Pearcy v. Stranahan and was finally resolved by the Hay-Quesada Treaty, which settled the status of people called pineros [pin-yeros]. This legislation prohibited a certain entity from entering into debt that it could not pay, or from making territorial concessions to anybody except the United States. This legislation was repealed by the Treaty of Relations, signed in 1934 as part of the Good Neighbor Policy, and it was cited as an example of imperialism by Fidel Castro. For 10 points, name this 1901 amendment named for a Connecticut Senator, which governed US-Cuban relations.

In this colony, Andrés Novales declared himself emperor after its governor, Mariano Fernández de Folgueras, threatened to limit the number of local-born soldiers. Anticolonial activists in this territory venerated a trio of martyred priests collectively known as the GOMBURZA. In this colony, the nonviolent pro-independence groups La Solidaridad and La Liga gradually gave way to a more radical movement led by Andres Bonifacio. Galleons traveling from this colony to Acapulco fueled the worldwide silver trade. In this colony, involvement in the pro-independence Katipunan (kah-tee-POO-nahn) society led to the execution of the author of El Filibusterismo (fil-ih-boost-er-EEZ-moh). For 10 points, name this modern-day country where Spanish rule was opposed by Jose Rizal and Emilio Aguinaldo.

William Fleetwood's attempt to measure this quantity in Chronicon Preciosum emerged out of a dispute about the fellowship rules of Oxford. Alberto Cavallo and Roberto Rigodon formed an MIT database used to publish a "Verdadera" number named for this quantity. A method named for Laspeyres produces higher estimates of this quantity than one named for Paasche. The Simpson-Bowles commission suggested using a "chained" form of a process used to measure this quantity to reduce substitution and small-sample biases. Market baskets are typically used to measure this quantity, whose core form excludes food and energy. For 10 points, name this quantity, measured by the CPI, which means that a given amount of money buys less goods.

Before the 2019 SI unit update, this value was obtained by measuring the speed of sound in argon at the temperature of the triple point of water. This value is the difference between specific heat at constant pressure and specific heat at constant volume. This value multiplies temperature and divides Faraday's constant in Nernst's equation. This value is often given in units of liter-atmospheres per mole-Kelvin. This value multiplies temperature and the natural log of the equilibrium constant to determine the Gibbs free energy change in a reaction. For 10 points, name this constant which is multiplied with "n" and "T" in the ideal gas law.

Seven seismologists in this nation are facing manslaughter charges for failing to predict a May 2009 earthquake. This nation's northern industrial regions lie at the south of what many call the "Blue Banana" of industry and include the Po River Valley, while the Apennine Mountains run through this nation which is also home to the Romagna region home to the cities of Parma and Ferrara. This nation controls the southeastern slopes of Mount Blanc and its capital lies on the Tiber River. For 10 points name this country with capital at Rome.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for lung volumes and capacities. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this diaphragm-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The diaphragm is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in lung volumes and capacities.

tossups.text: One of these beings is represented in the Womb Realm by the Wisdom King Gundari, while another of these beings made the forty-eight vows, in which he promises to appear before anyone who calls upon him at the moment of death. The most famous of these persons declared that, "all is burning," in the Fire Sermon, which is included in the Pali Canon. The Pure Land Sect worships the Amitahba form of this being, while another form of this being espoused the Four Noble Truths. With a name meaning "Enlightened One," For 10 points, name these figures, which include one who was born Siddhartha Gautama.

One of his last stories depicts a creature from Lithuania who is half-bear, half-man. In another, a statue of Venus seems to have killed the protagonist and driven his fiancée insane. His early works include plays about the Jacquerie and the family of Carvajal, the latter of which is a retelling of The Cenci, while he wrote about the Saint Bartholomew's Day Massacre in his novel Chronicle of the Reign of Charles IX. His collection Mosaic includes a story about a revolt on a slave ship, "Tamango," and another about a Corsican youth who is killed by his own father, "Mateo Falcone," though he is better known for a novella about a woman who prods her brother Orso Antonio to avenge their father. In addition to "Columba," he wrote an tale in which an archaeologist listens to the story of a bandit who killed the woman he loved. FTP, name this French author of The Theater of Clara Gazul and a work about Don José and his gypsy lover, Carmen.

According to Pausanias, one of this woman's daughters was the first woman to marry twice, wedding both Perieres of Messina and Oebalus of Laconia. Some sources claim that she was originally betrothed to Agenor, the twin brother of Belus, while others claim that her fiance was Belus's son Phineus. Ovid claims that corals first appeared as part of a story involving this woman, who met her eventual husband in a manner similar to the later story of Hesione and Heracles. This woman's mother asserted that she was far more beautiful than the Nereids, prompting Poseidon to send Cetus to ravage Ethiopia. She was saved from a would-be sacrifice by a hero who had recently acquired Medusa's head. For 10 points, name this daughter of Cepheus and Cassiopeia who was chained naked to a rock in the sea until her rescue by Perseus.

In one story concerning this fairy tale character, her tears are able to cure a blinded prince. A deal is made to trade this girl for rampion, stolen by her parents, with a neighboring enchantress. For 10 points, name this Brothers Grimm fairy tale character that is called to "let down your hair."

Rulers of this civilization were called Tlatoani in the Nahuatl language. This civilization once fought a Flower War against its neighbors, and a ruler of this civilization saw the "night of sorrows" against an invader of this civilization. The leader of those invaders called the capital city of this civilization the "Venice of the West" due to its canal system. That city, Tenochtitlan, was the home of Emperors Montezuma I & II. For 10 points, name this central american civilization conquered by Hernan Cortes.

The phrase "that they all may be one" is taken from the end of this book's High Priestly Prayer, part of the Farewell Discourse. The main text of this book is divided into the Hymn to the World, the Book of Signs, and the Book of Glory. The image of Jesus as the Lamb of God originated in this book, whose assumed author is identified in the text as "the disciple whom Jesus loved." This book was likely inspired by Philo of Alexandria's account of the logos [LOH-gohs] for its opening phrase "In the beginning was the Word." The only non-synoptic canonical gospel is, for 10 points, what book which is typically placed after Matthew, Mark, and Luke.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for axial skeleton bones. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this skull-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The skull is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in axial skeleton bones.

parts.text: Identify this class of supervised learning methods from statistical machine learning. It takes its name from those elements of the data which lie on one of the hyperplanes.
A typical use of an SVM is for this task, in which data must be sorted into a number of pre-trained categories.
Classification may also be performed using this method, in which a prior probability is multiplied by a class likelihood and divided by the evidence to obtain a posterior probability.

bonuses.leadin: Methods of this type maximize the margins around a hyperplane that divides the data. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these devices that measure the heat produced by chemical reactions. When using these devices, you typically take the temperature change and multiply by the specific heat and mass.

Isothermal titration calorimetry can be used in this branch of chemistry to determine the needed amounts of starting reagent to reach the midpoint. In general, this branch of chemistry uses chemical equations to find the proper ratios of start reactants to achieve desired product.
In this variant of calorimetry, the heat capacity of a sample is measured as a function of temperature. The thermal transitions of a polymer can be determined using this technique.

bonuses.leadin: The constant-volume type of this device is also known as the "bomb" type. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Besides degrees, name one other unit for measuring angles.
Given that pi radians are equal to 180 degrees, convert 120 degrees to radians. Exact value in terms of pi, or decimal value rounded to two decimal places, are each acceptable.
One degree is divided into 60 of these units, which are themselves divided into seconds.

bonuses.leadin: At least one part of this bonus requires computation. For 10 points each, answer these questions about angles:

parts.text: Name this American composer of Essay for Orchestra and Vanessa.
Barber is probably best known for this tragic work, an arrangement of the second movement of his first String Quartet.
Barber's first major work for orchestra was an Overture to this play by Richard Brinsley Sheridan.

bonuses.leadin: Though a traditionalist composer in most respects, he occasionally incorporated popular music into pieces like Excursions and A Hand of Bridge. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this situation commonly studied in game theory in which two players can both either defect or stay loyal to each other.
In the prisoner's dilemma, this situation occurs when both players decide to defect, since no player stands to gain by changing their strategy.

In the related stag-hunt game, if both players choose to cooperate and hunt the stag, they achieve this condition, which occurs when one player cannot gain value without the other player losing value.

bonuses.leadin: This scenario was first devised by Flood and Dresher in 1950. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this mutual defense alliance between the US and most of Western Europe, which was created in 1948.
In this plan, named for the American Secretary of State, the US gave monetary aid to devastated European economies. The USSR refused its aid for Eastern Europe, fearing US influence.
This American president supported the Marshall Plan. His namesake doctrine dealt with forcibly stopping the spread of communism.

bonuses.leadin: It is often considered the Western European counterpart to the Warsaw Pact. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this country where a civil war pitted the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front against the ruling ARENA party. This country's leader Roberto D'Aubuisson ordered the assassination of Óscar Romero.
The Salvadoran Civil war was sparked by the murder of Romero, who belonged to this religious institution. This institution has the largest following of any religious institution in Latin America.
acceptableAnswers: accept word forms such as Roman Catholicism

parts.text: The FMLN were inspired by this party's victory in a nearby civil war against the Contras the year earlier, after which they overthrew Anastasio Somoza. This Nicaraguan party is currently led by Daniel Ortega.
acceptableAnswers: accept Frente Sandinista de Liberación Nacional

bonuses.leadin: An American trained army in this country's civil war massacred hundreds of civilians in the 1981 El Mozote massacre. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The dynastic crisis began after this homosexual emperor unsurprisingly failed to produce an heir. His lover, Dong Xian, attempted to seize power after his death.

After the empire ran through a few more emperors, mostly infants, this usurper seized power. He imposed a new system of weights and measures and founded the Xin Dynasty, which fell to rebels after a flood of the Yellow River.
After the fall of Wang Mang, China was reunited under a restoration of this dynasty. This dynasty succeeded the Qin and was founded by Liu Bang in the 3rd century BCE.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about a dynastic crisis in 1st century China. For 10 points each:

parts.text: In George Peele's "The Araygnement of Paris", this goddess proposes the nymph Eliza, who rules the Angeli in Elysium, and not Juno, Pallas, or Venus receive the golden ball from Paris in a sort of apotheosis of Elizabeth.

Elizabeth is often identified with Cynthia, the virginal moon who unites the couples in Act V of this John Lyly play. The title character is drugged to sleep for decades, unlike in a Keats poem, when the moon puts him to sleep.

Some scholars have also seen an allegory of Elizabeth in the queen who defeats Venus and adopts Cupid in this early Lyly comedy, which also has a major theme of time's inexorable march, as seen in the character of Sybilla.

bonuses.leadin: Identify the following about allegorical appearances of Elizabeth I in Elizabethan drama, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this economic problem, which asks why returns on stocks are far higher than returns on Treasury bonds, and why more investors don't buy stocks with higher returns instead of Treasury bonds.

This author of the textbook Macroeconomics: A Modern Approach built on the work of Thomas Rietz to explain the equity premium puzzle in his paper "Rare Disasters and Asset Markets in the Twentieth Century." In a 1991 paper, this economist listed his namesake variables and analyzed their correlation with income growth.
For many of his ideas regarding the slashing of taxes to curtail government revenue, Barro cites this author of Capitalism and Freedom who worked with Anna Schwartz on a monetary history of the US.

bonuses.leadin: This result was first hypothesized in a 1985 paper by Rajnish Mehra and Edward C. Prescott, who explained it by positing that investors are more risk-averse than commonly assumed. FTPE:

parts.text: Give this term for properties that depend on the amount of solute rather than properties of the solute.
This colligative property is defined as the pressure that must be applied to a solution to stop fluid movement across a semi·permeable membrane.
In Raoult's law, this quantity is multiplied by the equilibrium vapor pressure of the component to calculate total vapor pressure, which is another colligative property.

bonuses.leadin: The elevation of boiling point and the depression of freezing point caused by adding solutes are both these types of properties. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this 20th-century social movement that sought to promote cultural and economic empowerment among Mexican Americans.
The Chicano blowouts were concentrated in this southern California city. During World War II, Hispanic residents of this city were targeted in the Zoot Suit Riots.
This Chicana activist worked with César Chavez to cofound the United Farm Workers. She coined the UFW's slogan, "Sí se puede" ("see say PWEH-day").

bonuses.leadin: In 1968, youth supporters of this movement staged a series of student strikes called its namesake "blowouts." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with limbic system.
What is the main function of the cerebrum in the nervous system?
Name another component of the nervous system related to limbic system.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human nervous system.

parts.text: Name this man. Althusser described an "epistemological break" between the "Young" and "Mature" works of this thinker in a book titled For [him], which examines a series of 1844 manuscripts that introduced his concept of "alienation."
The aforementioned Althusser work is a "Reading" of this unfinished volume by Marx, which is subtitled "A Critique of Political Economy."

Althusser considered Marx's break from Young to Mature to coincide with his split with this other thinker. Marx wrote a set of 11 short observations titled for this man that criticizes materialists as objective and idealist.

bonuses.leadin: Louis Althusser was the primary author of a book titled "Reading" a work by this man. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this play in which a deranged man attempts to rape Lulu during a blackout that follows a game of Blind Man's Bluff.
The Birthday Party was written by this English dramatist of The Dumb Waiter.

The term "comedy of menace" was taken from the title of a play by David Campton, who mentored this other prolific English playwright. This "master of farce" wrote the plays Private Fears in Public Places and Absurd Person Singular.

bonuses.leadin: This play led the critic Irving Wardle to introduce the term "comedy of menace." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this figure who wields the spear Gáe Bulg ("guy bolg"). This figure singlehandedly defeated the armies of Queen Medb ("mayv") at the Cattle Raid of Cooley.

Original language term required. Cú Chulainn is spiritually weakened after he eats a meal offered to him by an old woman, thus allowing Lugaid to kill him and breaking one of these taboos in Irish myth.
The meal the old woman offered Cú Chulainn was the meat of these animals, thus breaking the geis placed upon him. Cerberus was a three-headed one of these animals in Greek myth.

bonuses.leadin: This figure dies after being struck by three spears fashioned by Lugaid ("LOO-gid"). For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this work, in which John the Savage hangs himself after rejecting Lenina, and Bernard and Helmholtz are exiled by the world controller Mustapha Mond.
In Brave New World, years are labeled after this automaker, who created the Model T and greatly improved the use of the assembly line.
This author of Brave New World also wrote about Walter Bidlake's affair with Lucy Tantamount in Point Counter Point.

bonuses.leadin: Human embryos are categorized in this novel by the Bokanovsky Process. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this 1803 "purchase" that resulted in the U.S. acquisition of territory on the west bank of the Mississippi, including the city of New Orleans.

The Jefferson administration sent a "Corps of Discovery" to explore the new territories. The expedition traveled up the Missouri River and crossed the northern Rockies under the leadership of these two men.
Lewis and Clark were helped on their journey by this Shoshone woman, the wife of a French-Canadian fur trader.

bonuses.leadin: James Monroe and Robert Livingston signed the treaty that carried out this transaction. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The Buddha's mother had a dream of an elephant of this color before his birth.
In Hinduism, Vishnu and some of his avatars have skin of this color. One important text to Zen Buddhism is the Cliff Record of this color.
Another Buddhist sect is called hats of this color. Also called the Gelug, the Dalai Lama leads this Tibetan Buddhist sect.

bonuses.leadin: Svetambara monks wear robes of this color. For 10 points each,

What is the main function of the phagocyte in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to complement system.
